title: M1: Vault browse (portable vault, part 1)
description:
Milestone M1 from roadmap.md: browse your REAL Bitwarden vault on the T-Embed color device.

Done when: unlock/browse your real vault on the color device (list + detail views), backed by companion-app push of real (decrypted) credentials.

Two pillars (largely parallel):
- Pillar A (on-device UI): credential list refinements + a new detail view designed for color + rotary encoder. M0 left on_activate unset in core/src/app.rs and explicitly deferred the detail view to M1/Uma. Also must solve the flagged problem: a sync landing mid-navigation must not blow away a pushed detail screen.
- Pillar B (companion app): a real companion that runs the Bitwarden SDK, authenticates, syncs, decrypts, and pushes real VaultItems over the existing HTTP+CBOR /api/sync push path (PushSyncSource already exists). Roadmap sanctions a CLI or simple desktop GUI for testing; full Web Vault integration deferred post-M2.

Kickoff phase = design (advisory, read-only): Uma (UX for list+detail), Ada (companion-app architecture + sync-vs-pushed-screen design), Fern (detail-view framework integration). Implementation children created after designs land.

title: M1: extract push-protocol wire crate
description: Extract Credential/SyncRequest/SyncResponse out of emulator/src/credentials into a new host-only push-protocol crate (serde + ciborium + uuid; NO dependency on bhk-core). Both emulator and the new companion depend on it so the CBOR /api/sync contract is defined once and cannot drift. From<Credential> for VaultItem stays in emulator (the only place that sees both crates). Per Ada's M1 architecture report.

title: M1: companion app - bw-CLI bridge
description: Host-only companion crate that bridges the official Bitwarden CLI (bw) to the device push path: shell out to bw list items, deserialize JSON, filter to login items (type==1), map to Credential (name, username, login.password, login.uris[0]->uri, notes, id), CBOR-encode a SyncRequest, POST to /api/sync. Depends on push-protocol for wire types + serde_json + a small blocking HTTP client (ureq). Verify field mapping against a real bw list items dump before finalizing. Record deliberate M1 omissions (totp, reprompt, folders, extra URIs). Per Ada's report; recommended over full Rust-SDK companion for time-to-real-data and demo credibility.

title: M1: VaultStore data model + no-rebuild App::step
description: Foundation for the M1 UI. Introduce a shared, App-owned VaultStore (items + SyncStatus) exposed to domain widgets via Rc<RefCell>, replacing the M0 shortcut where App::step rebuilds the whole Navigator on every sync (core/src/app.rs:92-100) and where VaultItem->ListItem drops the id (app.rs:18-20). App::step becomes: pull latest snapshot, write into store, set dirty on change - and NEVER rebuild the Navigator. Safe because step (borrow_mut) and render (borrow) are strictly sequential phases of the run loop, single-threaded. SyncStatus for M1 derived in App from sync() Result + item count (Synced/Error/Empty); richer Syncing/Offline deferred (no SyncSource trait change). GATED on the vault-store-data-ownership ADR. Per Fern's framework report (B1).

title: M1: CredentialListView (store-backed, activate->detail)
description: Domain list widget reading the VaultStore live: selection tracked by VaultItem id (re-resolve to index after a store change, clamp if id vanished, so a background sync does not jump the cursor). on_activate builds the detail Screen bound to the selected id + store handle. Content-region empty/syncing/error states from store status + item count. Right-edge scrollbar. Full-row focus fill + 3px left accent bar (shared draw_focus_block helper). Retires the ad-hoc list + id-dropping projection in app.rs. Per Uma (UX) + Fern (B2).

title: M1: dynamic chrome (title/readout/status dot/contextual hint)
description: Add a Widget::chrome_contribution hook (title override, position readout, contextual hint) merged by Screen::render over the static title/hint. Thread app-global SyncStatus into render for a title-bar status dot. Slotted title bar: clip the title to its sub-rect (retire the un-clipped single-blob title at screen.rs:157-162) and right-align the 3/42 readout using font metrics, not a hardcoded px/char (survives the later u8g2-fonts swap). Per Fern (B3) + Uma. Depends on the VaultStore foundation; readout/hint sources land with the list/detail widgets.

title: M1: CredentialDetailView + SecretField (new detail screen)
description: New single-container detail view (Flavor 2: one focusable widget managing field focus internally, so it dodges the both-fire navigator footgun and can render a cohesive gone-state). Fields: USERNAME, PASSWORD, WEBSITE (if Some), NOTES (if Some), read live from the store by id. SecretField: masked as a fixed count of dots (not true length - no length leak), amber cleartext when revealed, reveal toggled on Activate, auto re-mask on FocusEvent::Lost. Field focus clamps (not wraps). Deleted-upstream -> store.get(id)==None -> gentle 'no longer in your vault' state with Back. Reserve (do NOT build) a per-field slot for M2 type-over-HID. Per Uma (UX) + Fern (B4).

title: M1: end-to-end verification (real bw vault -> device browse)
description: Tess: prove the M1 done-condition end to end. Run the companion against a real bw-unlocked vault, push over /api/sync, and browse list + detail on the device in headless (agent-driven, screenshot-inspected) and windowed (screencapture) modes. Verify: list renders real credentials, activate opens detail, password reveal/re-mask works, Back returns with selection preserved, and a re-push mid-detail does not yank the user out. Zoomed/live inspection per rendering-verification discipline. Real-hardware run folds into the on-hardware verification bead when boards arrive.

title: On-device first-class client via PRIVATE FORK of Bitwarden SDK (DEFERRED)
description:
DEFERRED / backlog. Revive ONLY if the companion-push concept validates and on-device decrypt is still wanted. Direction: PRIVATE fork (NOT upstream) -- rationale (Andreas, 2026-08-11): side project; feature-flag swaps for embedded impls likely never ship in production, so it should not add cost to Bitwarden's real SDK.

Requires solving THREE independent fronts (per spike ai-bitwarden-hw-key-8d7.2):
1. SDK non-modularity + transport: fork bitwarden-api-base/-core/-key-connector to inject an esp-idf/mbedtls transport (no seam today; they use reqwest::Client directly). Also feature-gate bitwarden-api-key-connector out of bitwarden-crypto so 'just the KDF' is depend-able.
2. ring-on-xtensa (NOT fixed by forking BW crates): ring's bundled C crypto links wrong-endian on xtensa-esp32s3-espidf (build.rs target detection). Options: patch ring's build.rs, or swap rustls to a pure-Rust RustCrypto crypto provider to drop ring (unverified on xtensa).
3. On-hardware validation: footprint (512KB SRAM / 8MB PSRAM), real PBKDF2/Argon2id latency, session-key fast path -- ALL still unmeasured (no physical board during the spike).

Reference artifact: throwaway spike branch 'bd-ai-bitwarden-hw-key-8d7.2' (pushed to origin) contains spike-sdk/ with the minimal repro + exact mitigations (ring 'less-safe-getrandom-espidf' feature; opt-level=0 for rustls/mockall). DO NOT delete that branch.

title: Fix host-build ergonomics: workspace default target esp32s3 forces --target everywhere
description:
Since W6 set .cargo/config.toml [build] target = xtensa-esp32s3-espidf as the WORKSPACE default, every host command (cargo build/test/run/clippy for emulator + bhk-core) fails unless you pass --target aarch64-apple-darwin (minifb/tiny_http can't cross-compile to xtensa; and cargo run would try espflash). Multiple agents + the user have tripped on this; the .cargo/config.toml comment wrongly claims the emulator is 'unaffected'. 

Fix options to weigh: (a) move the esp32s3 default into firmware/.cargo/config.toml (per-dir) and leave the workspace root defaulting to host, so / and  'just work' and firmware builds from its dir or with explicit --target; (b) add cargo aliases (e.g. ) ; (c) keep global esp32s3 but fix the misleading comment + document the --target requirement prominently in README. Recommend (a): day-to-day dev is the emulator, so the ergonomic default should be host. Also correct the false comment at .cargo/config.toml:5-6.

title: M0: Platform Migration (T-Embed color + rotary, hardware-portable foundation)
description:
Green-field rebuild of the UI framework + app architecture for the Lilygo T-Embed (ESP32-S3, 320x170 color ST7789, rotary encoder), hardware-portable, first-class-Bitwarden-client direction. Synthesizes Ada's architecture design and Fern's UI-framework design.

KEY DECISIONS (orchestrator-reconciled from Ada + Fern):
- Platform-free 'core' crate; hardware injected behind a Platform boundary (Display/Input/Clock/Storage).
- Single generic main loop replaces the two divergent loops (main.rs vs bin/desktop.rs).
- Shared in-RAM Rgb565 framebuffer is the single render output; 3 run modes differ only at final flush -> headless screenshot faithful to device by construction.
- Rgb565 canonical throughout core (RESOLVED conflict: Ada proposed RGB888; Fern's Rgb565 wins for 3-mode fidelity). Core bound to Error=Infallible; mipidsi error absorbed at device surface.
- Retire BOTH GUI engines: src/gui/ is dead code (all call sites commented out); src/simple_gui/ custom RGBA rasterizer blocks color. Salvage concepts only (nav stack, ComponentAction, FocusEvent) reimplemented on embedded-graphics.
- Rotary-encoder NavIntent vocabulary (Next/Prev/NextN/Activate/Back) replaces 3-button KeyCode. Encoder-only for the M0 shell; keep intent seam for future button driver.
- SyncSource seam decouples app from the SDK spike; PushSyncSource (existing HTTP+CBOR) is fallback/dev aid, SdkSyncSource behind the spike.
- OSS: adopt embedded-graphics + embedded-graphics-framebuf + mipidsi + u8g2-fonts + light embedded-layout; defer embedded-menu to M1; reject slint/lvgl and SDL2 simulator.

DONE WHEN (roadmap.md M0): empty-but-real 320x170 color shell, encoder-drivable, running identically in all three modes (headless/windowed/real-target); SDK spike delivers a go/no-go + ADR.

comments.author: Andreas Coroiu
comments.text:
PROGRESS 1/3: Set up spike-sdk/ (throwaway, xtensa-esp32s3-espidf, ESP-IDF v5.3.3, reusing existing .embuild toolchain via symlink to dodge a Zscaler TLS-interception issue with Python's cert store that blocked fresh esp-idf tool installs).

FINDING A (ring/rustls, real bug + real fix): Just adding bitwarden-crypto as a dependency (no networking touched directly) transitively pulls in reqwest+rustls+ring via bitwarden-crypto -> bitwarden-api-key-connector. Initial build failed: ring 0.17.14's SystemRandom does not implement rustls's required SecureRandom trait on this target -> 9 compile errors in rustls-0.23.43/src/crypto/ring/*.rs (e.g. 'the trait bound SystemRandom: ring::rand::sealed::SecureRandom is not satisfied'). Root cause confirmed by reading ring-0.17.14/src/rand.rs: target_os=espidf IS supported by ring, but only behind ring's own opt-in feature 'less-safe-getrandom-espidf' (ring/src/rand.rs:126), which is NOT enabled by default when rustls pulls ring in transitively. FIX: adding an explicit 'ring = { version = "0.17", features = ["less-safe-getrandom-espidf"] }' to Cargo.toml forces the feature on via Cargo feature unification (ring is a single shared dependency in the graph) -> ring+rustls then compile cleanly for xtensa-esp32s3-espidf. So: ring/rustls CAN be made to build on esp-idf, it just needs this one non-obvious feature flag. Good news for the TLS sub-question.

FINDING B (new blocker, unrelated to TLS): after fixing ring, build now fails on mockall v0.15.0 with an opaque 'error: Undefined temporary symbol' (LLVM/assembler-level error, no source location) when rustc targets xtensa-esp32s3-espidf. Confirmed via 'cargo tree -i mockall': mockall is pulled in by bitwarden-api-key-connector (crates/bitwarden-api-key-connector/Cargo.toml) as an UNCONDITIONAL, non-optional, non-dev dependency (not feature gated). bitwarden-api-key-connector is itself an unconditional dependency of bitwarden-crypto. So there is no way to depend on 'just bitwarden-crypto' (KDF/crypto primitives) without also pulling in mockall, reqwest, reqwest-middleware, and tokio (full/default features) -- the entire HTTP/API-client stack rides along even when you only want the crypto primitives. mockall itself then hits what looks like an xtensa-LLVM backend codegen bug (reproduced in isolation via 'cargo build -p mockall --target xtensa-esp32s3-espidf', same error in both debug and release profiles). This blocks forward progress on footprint/KDF/session-key measurements via the real bitwarden-crypto crate as currently structured.

comments.author: Andreas Coroiu
comments.text:
PROGRESS 2/3: Isolated the TLS stack (reqwest+rustls+rustls-platform-verifier+tokio) from the mockall blocker by temporarily dropping bitwarden-crypto from Cargo.toml. rustls itself (independent of bitwarden, independent of mockall) hit the SAME 'error: Undefined temporary symbol' xtensa-LLVM codegen bug found in mockall -- confirmed via 'cargo build -p rustls --release -v' targeting xtensa-esp32s3-espidf. WORKAROUND FOUND: adding '[profile.release.package.rustls] opt-level = 0' (and same for mockall) avoids the bug -- this looks like an xtensa-LLVM backend optimizer bug, not something either crate does wrong. Re-enabled bitwarden-crypto with both mitigations (ring/less-safe-getrandom-espidf feature + opt-level=0 overrides for rustls+mockall) and got PAST compilation for the first time, all the way to the final link step.

FINDING C (the decisive blocker, exactly the risk flagged in the bead): the combined image fails at LINK time with a genuine ring bug: 'ld: ...libring-*.rlib(a0330e891e733f4e-gfp_p384.o): compiled for a big endian system and target is little endian' / 'ld: cross-endian linking for ...(curve25519.o) not supported', repeated across gfp_p384.o, p256.o, limbs.o, mem.o, poly1305.o, ecp_nistz.o, curve25519.o. Root cause: ring's build.rs compiles its bundled C crypto sources via the 'cc' crate, and its target-arch detection does not have a correct entry for xtensa-esp32s3-espidf, so it ends up invoking the xtensa-esp-elf-gcc cross-compiler with the wrong endianness assumption for at least some of its C translation units, producing object files that cannot be linked against the rest of the (correctly little-endian) xtensa binary. This is a ring-crate limitation (ring has never had official xtensa support), not something fixable from the SDK or app side without patching ring's own build.rs. Confirms the bead's top hypothesis: 'ring's per-arch assembly likely won't build for xtensa' -- it manifests as a cross-endian C-object link failure rather than a missing-assembly-file error, but the practical result is identical: ring cannot be linked for this target as currently pulled in by the SDK.

Compounding structural finding: bitwarden-crypto (meant to be 'just the crypto/KDF primitives') has an UNCONDITIONAL, non-optional dependency on bitwarden-api-key-connector (crates/bitwarden-api-key-connector/Cargo.toml), which itself unconditionally depends on mockall + reqwest + reqwest-middleware + tokio. There is no Cargo feature to opt out. So you cannot depend on 'just the KDF' from this SDK without also pulling in, and successfully linking, its full HTTP/TLS/mocking stack. And bitwarden-api-base (crates/bitwarden-api-base/Cargo.toml) hard-wires reqwest+rustls+rustls-platform-verifier for all non-wasm targets with no seam to substitute a different HTTP/TLS client -- routing through esp-idf/mbedtls instead of rustls would require forking bitwarden-api-base (and likely bitwarden-core, bitwarden-api-api, bitwarden-api-identity, bitwarden-api-key-connector) since they use reqwest::Client directly, not behind a trait.

CAVEAT (environment): no physical T-Embed / ESP32-S3 hardware is attached to this dev machine (checked /dev/tty.*, /dev/cu.*, USB device list -- none found). Even where compilation succeeded, no on-device flashing/timing/footprint measurement was possible. Real link/footprint/KDF-latency numbers require someone with the physical board. For rough context only (NOT representative of ESP32-S3 Xtensa LX7 @ 240MHz + PSRAM), I ran the exact pinned KDF crate versions bitwarden-crypto uses (pbkdf2 0.13.0-rc.10, argon2 0.6.0-rc.8) on the host dev machine: PBKDF2-SHA256 600k iters = 41.9ms, Argon2id 64MiB/3-iter/4-lane (Bitwarden's default client KDF params) = 87.2ms, both on host CPU (Apple Silicon class), not ESP32-S3. Host-to-embedded scaling for this workload is commonly 1-2 orders of magnitude slower on Xtensa LX7 for the PBKDF2/SHA2 hashing itself, and Argon2id's 64MiB working set would have to live in PSRAM (SPI-attached, far lower bandwidth than internal SRAM), which is likely to dominate its cost beyond simple clock-scaling -- this is a hypothesis, not a measurement.

comments.author: Andreas Coroiu
comments.text:
GO/NO-GO RECOMMENDATION (evidence-based, see PROGRESS 1-2 comments for full detail and exact error text):

NO-GO on 'SDK does its own on-device TLS/HTTP directly (reqwest+rustls) for sync', as currently structured, for xtensa-esp32s3-espidf. Evidence: reproducible LINK failure -- ring's bundled C crypto objects (gfp_p384.o, p256.o, curve25519.o, poly1305.o, ecp_nistz.o, mem.o, limbs.o) compile with the wrong endianness for this target and fail to link ('cross-endian linking...not supported'). This is a ring build.rs/target-detection limitation with no known app-side fix, compounded by an xtensa-LLVM optimizer bug that separately breaks rustls/mockall at nonzero opt-levels (workaroundable, but signals xtensa Rust toolchain immaturity for this class of dependency). Additionally, bitwarden-crypto cannot be depended on in isolation -- it unconditionally pulls the same broken reqwest/rustls/ring stack (plus mockall) via bitwarden-api-key-connector, so even 'just use the SDK's crypto/KDF, roll your own transport' is not possible without a fork.

The only path to make the real Bitwarden Rust SDK work on this hardware would be forking bitwarden-api-base/-core/-api/-identity/-key-connector to replace reqwest+rustls with an esp-idf/mbedtls-backed HTTP client (no existing seam for this) AND getting a working ring replacement or patching ring's build.rs for xtensa -- both are non-trivial, ongoing-maintenance forks of Bitwarden's own 'internal, do not use' crates, not a build-flag change.

RECOMMENDATION: for M1, do NOT plan on-device SDK-driven sync/decrypt via the real bitwarden-crypto/bitwarden-core crates as currently published. The push-fallback direction (server/companion pushes already-decrypted or device-specific-encrypted data to the device, device does no TLS/HTTP/full-SDK work) remains the only demonstrated-feasible sync direction from this spike. If on-device SDK sync is still wanted long-term, treat it as a much larger, separate initiative: (a) fork+maintain patched bitwarden-api-base with a custom transport, (b) get ring (or an alternative RustCrypto-only rustls provider, if one exists) working on xtensa, (c) revisit only after both are proven in isolation.

NOT ANSWERED (blocked by the above + no physical hardware attached to this dev machine): footprint fit in 512KB SRAM/8MB PSRAM, real on-device PBKDF2/Argon2id latency, session-key fast-path prototype/timing. These all require a working link (not achieved) and/or a flashed device (none available here). Host-CPU-only reference numbers for the two KDFs are in the prior comment, explicitly flagged as non-representative.

Spike branch (throwaway, not for merge): bd-ai-bitwarden-hw-key-8d7.2, pushed to origin. spike-sdk/ contains the minimal repro (Cargo.toml shows the exact ring feature + opt-level mitigations; Cargo.lock pins the exact bitwarden-crypto git rev and dependency versions used).

comments.text:
APPROACH: Converted single crate to a 3-member workspace (core/firmware/emulator) per the ADR. Structural calls made beyond the literal ADR text:
1. core package named 'bhk-core' (not literally 'core') to avoid crate-name collision with the sysroot 'core' crate under an --extern path dependency; directory is still core/ per the ADR.
2. The old GUI engines (gui/, simple_gui/) are duplicated between firmware/ and emulator/ rather than centralized, since both binaries need them and the bead explicitly forbids putting them in bhk-core. Pruned emulator's copy of gui/ down to just the input submodule (InputInterface/KeyCode/InputEvent) since emulator never uses the rest of the old engine (document/layout/render/style/primitives/icons) -- only firmware's view.rs exercises the full old engine. simple_gui/ + simple_view.rs are duplicated in full (both bins use them).
3. firmware no longer carries the wire-format credentials module at all (dropped entirely) -- nothing in firmware ever consumed Credential/SyncRequest/SyncResponse. That wire format now lives only in emulator/src/credentials/mod.rs, with new From<Credential>/From<&Credential> impls converting to bhk_core::VaultItem at the HTTP/storage boundary (emulator/src/main.rs).
4. core::input::NavIntent, core::platform::{DisplaySurface,InputSource,Clock,Storage,FrameBuffer565}, core::sync_source::{SyncSource,UnlockToken} added as placeholder/trait-only seams per the ADRs -- no implementations, no SdkSyncSource (per instructions).

comments.text:
CORRECTION to my earlier VERIFY comment (Tess): user caught a real defect in the render_scene.png evidence that I signed off on too quickly at low zoom. Amending verdict.

ROOT CAUSE (confirmed, not a guess): core/src/render/list.rs lines 186-221 (VerticalList::render).

- ROW_HEIGHT = 20px (line 55).
- Label drawn at baseline y = row_top + 12 (line 209).
- Sublabel drawn at baseline y = row_top + 12 + 9 = row_top + 21 (line 217).
- Font is FONT_6X10 (embedded-graphics 0.8.2, src/mono_font/generated/ascii.rs:64-75): character_size height = 10, baseline = 7 → glyph descent below baseline = 10 - 7 = 3px.
- `Text::new` with the default TextStyle uses Baseline::Alphabetic (embedded-graphics src/text/text_style.rs:55) — i.e. the y coordinate passed IS the baseline row, glyphs extend baseline-7 to baseline+3.

So the sublabel glyph box spans [row_top+21-7, row_top+21+3] = [row_top+14, row_top+24]. The row itself only spans [row_top, row_top+20). The sublabel overflows the row's own 20px band by 4px, into the next row's territory. Rows are drawn top-to-bottom in the same loop (line 185 `for (index, item) in self.items.iter().enumerate()`), so row N+1's selection-highlight fill rect (drawn at the start of its own iteration, line 204) paints over that 4px overflow from row N — this is exactly the "selection box looks offset" artifact the user spotted: the box is positioned correctly per the row grid, but it visibly eats the bottom of the previous row's sublabel because that sublabel was never confined to its own row in the first place. Where the next row isn't selected (no fill), the overflow is simply left visible, bleeding into the next row's blank space — the "text overlapping" the user saw.

Confirmed visually: zoomed render_scene.png (4x, via `sips -z 680 1280`) shows the purple selection box cutting a hard horizontal line straight through "alice@example.com" (row 0's sublabel, overwritten by row 1's selection fill), and "alice-dev" (row 1's sublabel) bleeding past the box's bottom edge before "AWS Console" starts.

Why the test suite didn't catch it: `core/tests/render_png_dump.rs::scene_renders_expected_chrome_colors` only asserts fill-rectangle background colors at 3 sample points (title bar, row-0 background, blank area below all rows) — it never samples pixels in the label/sublabel text region, so glyph-level vertical overflow between rows is invisible to it.

This is IN the exact code (list.rs) this bead was verifying, not a pre-existing/unrelated issue. My original "PNG shows a real rendered scene... matches expectations exactly" was true at the level I checked (regions present, correct row selected) but I did not zoom in far enough to catch the sub-row-level defect. Correcting per epistemic-honesty standard rather than standing by the premature GO.

AMENDED VERDICT: NO-GO as-is. The render core's row layout math (list.rs:207-221) needs the sublabel baseline offset fixed to fit within ROW_HEIGHT given FONT_6X10's real metrics (e.g. label baseline ~row_top+9, sublabel baseline ~row_top+18, or increase ROW_HEIGHT) before this merges, plus a pixel-sampling test at a sublabel coordinate (e.g. within [row_top+14, row_top+20)) to catch this class of bug in the future. Everything else in my original VERIFY (build/tests/boundary/clippy) still stands as reported.

comments.text: APPROACH: core/src/render/navigator.rs Navigator::render() never cleared the target framebuffer before drawing. Undetected until now because every existing test/example allocated a fresh (black) FrameBuffer565 per render call. App/run reuse a single long-lived framebuffer across frames (per the presentation-surface ADR's explicit design), which exposed it: VerticalList only paints a background fill for the currently-selected row, so moving selection away from a row left its old highlight pixels behind. Fixed with target.clear(Rgb565::BLACK) at the top of Navigator::render; added a regression test (rendering_into_the_same_framebuffer_twice_does_not_leave_the_previous_frames_selection_highlight_behind).

title: Fix: windowed emulator renders a blank window (no per-frame minifb update)
description:
SEVERITY: M0 emulator shell is unusable in windowed mode (the human-facing mode). Follow-up to W7 (ai-bitwarden-hw-key-8d7.9).

VISUAL PROOF: launched `./target/aarch64-apple-darwin/debug/desktop` (windowed) from main, screencaptured — the 'Bitwarden HW Key - Desktop Emulator' window opens but renders COMPLETELY BLANK (uniform dark; no Vault title bar, list, or hint bar). The same App renders correctly via HeadlessSurface PNG, so App/render/framebuffer are fine — this is windowed-present-only.

ROOT CAUSE: nothing calls minifb Window::update() per frame. WindowedInput::poll() (emulator/src/platform/input.rs:71-86) reads is_key_down()/get_scroll_wheel() WITHOUT first calling window.update() (minifb requires update() to refresh input state AND to pump/paint the window). MinifbSurface::flush() (minifb_surface.rs:100-109) calls update_with_buffer() but only on dirty frames (run.rs:72). So the window gets a single update_with_buffer on frame 1 and is never pumped again -> macOS never composites it -> blank; input is also dead.

FIX (confined to emulator; do NOT change bhk_core::run or the Platform traits): call window.update() every frame in windowed mode. Cleanest is in WindowedInput::poll(): borrow_mut, window.update(), then read is_key_down/get_scroll_wheel (this is also correct minifb usage - update() must precede input reads). MinifbSurface::flush() continues pushing new pixels via update_with_buffer on dirty frames. Frame 1: poll's update() (empty), then dirty flush's update_with_buffer shows the shell; subsequent frames: poll's update() keeps it alive + responsive.

VERIFICATION: orchestrator (main thread, has Screen Recording permission) relaunches the windowed binary and screencaptures to confirm the Vault shell renders + selection moves on arrow keys. Subagents cannot see a window, so windowed-visual verification is an orchestrator responsibility going forward (relates to bead ai-bitwarden-hw-key-dvm / three-mode testability).

comments.author: Andreas Coroiu
comments.text: LEARNED: minifb requires Window::update() (or update_with_buffer()) unconditionally every frame -- it both pumps native window events (needed for macOS to keep compositing/painting) and refreshes is_key_down()/get_scroll_wheel() state. In a Platform-generic loop that only flushes on dirty frames, the InputSource::poll() call (which runs every frame regardless of dirty state) is the right place to own that pump, not the DisplaySurface::flush() call.

title: Real-target (on-device) verification strategy — DEFERRED until T-Embed ships
description: The real device is NOT directly agent-controllable the way headless/windowed emulator modes are (agent can't physically turn the rotary encoder or read the ST7789 framebuffer). The three-mode ADR's 'real-target' mode needs a concrete verify path. Likely direction to evaluate: reuse the SAME seams the headless mode uses — NavIntent injection + framebuffer capture — but transport them over serial/USB so an agent can drive the physical device and read back its Rgb565 framebuffer as a PNG for visual verification. Alternatives to weigh: on-device serial logging of UI state (text), a framebuffer-dump-over-serial, an on-device self-test mode, or human-in-the-loop (photograph screen + manual encoder). Owners: Tess (three run modes) + Ruby (firmware seam), input from Ada/Fern on the seam. REVISIT when the physical T-Embed arrives (hardware in transit). Blocks fully closing M0's 'drivable on the T-Embed' done-criterion.

title: Firmware: support both T-Embed variants (plain + CC1101)
description: Support both ordered boards behind a build-time board-config selection. Plain T-Embed (primary): encoder A/B/BTN on GPIO2/GPIO1/GPIO0. T-Embed CC1101: encoder on GPIO4/GPIO5/GPIO0 plus an independent user button on GPIO6 (candidate for a dedicated Back later). App/UI stays board-agnostic via NavIntent; this is pin-map + optional extra-button plumbing only, no runtime auto-detection. Firmware GPIO0 = encoder press is also the ESP32-S3 BOOT strap (hold-during-power-on enters download mode) - account for this in any hold-to-X UX. Build-only until physical boards arrive; real verification folds into the on-hardware verification effort. Sources captured in research: LilyGo factory pin_config.h (plain) and T-Embed-CC1101 utilities.h/pinmap.
